coverage_guards.reason: CSV has no syntax for saying that its first row is a header. The Pack reads the first row's cells as column names only where a cell begins with a letter or an underscore, so a file whose first row is numbers, dates or empty declares no columns at all, and a headerless file whose first data row is textual declares that row as its columns.

Cell values in data rows are not stated. The grammar gives a cell its position in the row and nothing else -- no role, no type and no link back to the header cell above it -- so a value carries no name that could resolve to anything, and stating one fact per cell would put one index row in the index for every cell of the file.

A column's ordinal is not stated. tree-sitter-csv names the first seven cells of a row first..seventh and then restarts the numbering inside remainder, so the node type of a cell does not identify its column beyond the seventh.

The delimiter in use is not stated. The grammar accepts comma, semicolon and pipe as anonymous tokens between cells; which one a file uses is visible in the tree but has no span that names anything, and quoted cells containing a delimiter are not re-split by this grammar.
